issues.legal_issue: Amounts raised from allottees under real estate projects are financial debts, making the allottees financial creditors in the corporate insolvency process.
material_facts: The proceedings concerned a corporate insolvency resolution process involving a real estate developer and claims by purchasers who had paid for homes.
An amendment deemed amounts raised from an allottee under a real estate project to have the commercial effect of borrowing.
issues.conclusion: Allottees with outstanding claims under real estate projects are financial creditors and must be included in the committee of creditors in accordance with the amended provisions.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5(7) and 5(8)(f) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, read with the explanation to Section 5(8)(f), amounts raised from allottees under real estate projects are deemed to be financial debt, and the allottees are financial creditors. Sections 7 and 21 provide for financial creditors to initiate the corporate insolvency resolution process and participate in the committee of creditors; Regulation 16A provides for representation of a class of creditors. No earlier cases were relied on for this interpretation.

predicates.corporate_insolvency_process: A corporate debtor is undergoing a corporate insolvency resolution process.
predicates.allottee_paid_amounts_under_real_estate_: A person allotted a home in a real estate project paid amounts to the developer.

issues.definition: When a corporate insolvency process concerns a project for which allottees paid amounts, those allottees are treated as financial creditors.

issues.legal_issue: An expired corporate insolvency resolution process may be recommenced to give effect to a material change that recognizes previously unrepresented home buyers as financial creditors.
material_facts: The corporate insolvency resolution process and its extended period had ended without an approved resolution plan.
When those periods expired, home buyers had no statutory status as financial creditors and no statutory voting rights in the committee of creditors.
An amendment recognizing home buyers as financial creditors came into force after the process period had expired.
The Court was already dealing with proceedings brought to protect home buyers, and their interests had been considered through interim directions.
issues.conclusion: The Court used its power under Article 142 to recommence the resolution process from the appointment of the interim resolution professional, allow a fresh statutory period, and require a newly constituted committee of creditors that included home buyers.
issues.legal_principle: Article 142 permits the Court, in the exceptional circumstances described, to do complete justice by recommencing the process for a fresh statutory period. The Court emphasized that the resolution must then proceed under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, including the amended provisions recognizing allottees as financial creditors, rather than under a court-created substitute process.

predicates.corporate_insolvency_proceeding: A corporate debtor is undergoing a corporate insolvency resolution proceeding.
predicates.resolution_period_expired_before_credito: The permitted resolution period ended before a legal change gave an affected creditor group financial-creditor status.
predicates.court_seised_to_protect_affected_credito: A court was already considering proceedings to protect the interests of the affected creditor group.

issues.definition: When the resolution period expires before a creditor group's status changes and a court is already considering protection of that group, the expired process may be restarted.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not replace the statutory insolvency resolution mechanism with a parallel court-supervised process for resolving a corporate debtor's affairs.
material_facts: The parties proposed that the Court appoint an independent committee to assess the developers' ability to complete the projects and to supervise a resolution outside the statutory process.
The statutory process assigns resolution decisions to insolvency professionals and the committee of creditors and requires specialized financial determinations.
The Court had decided to recommence the corporate insolvency resolution process under the statutory framework.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to appoint a committee to oversee a resolution outside the statutory process and required the resolution to follow the statutory insolvency framework.
issues.legal_principle: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, establishes a market-driven process that assigns responsibility to the resolution professional and committee of creditors and gives primacy to their commercial decisions. The Court held that its power to do complete justice should not be used to supplant those statutory mechanisms with a court-directed process.

predicates.corporate_insolvency_proceeding: A corporate debtor is undergoing a corporate insolvency resolution proceeding.
predicates.statutory_expert_resolution_mechanism_ex: A statutory process assigns the resolution work and relevant decisions to designated insolvency professionals and creditor representatives.
predicates.parallel_court_supervised_process_propos: A party proposes that a court create and supervise a separate resolution process outside the statutory mechanism.

issues.definition: When an insolvency proceeding has a statutory expert resolution mechanism and a separate court-supervised process is proposed, the separate process is declined.

issues.legal_issue: A person barred from being a resolution applicant, including a connected person to whom the statutory disqualifications apply, cannot participate in the corporate insolvency resolution process.
material_facts: The holding company and the corporate debtor's promoters sought to participate in the resolution process.
The Court found that statutory disqualifications applied to them, including disqualifications concerning non-performing asset accounts and specified transactions.
The proposed participants lacked the demonstrated financial capacity to complete the unfinished projects.
The resolution process was being recommenced and the Court declined to make an exception for the former promoters.
issues.conclusion: The corporate debtor, its holding company, and their promoters were ineligible to participate in the resolution process.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, bars persons meeting its disqualification criteria, including specified persons connected with them, from acting as resolution applicants. Section 30(4), as amended, prevents the committee of creditors from approving a plan submitted by an ineligible applicant. The Court relied on Parliament's stated purpose of preventing persons whose conduct contributed to defaults, or who were otherwise undesirable, from regaining control through the resolution process.

predicates.corporate_insolvency_proceeding: A corporate debtor is undergoing a corporate insolvency resolution proceeding.
predicates.applicant_or_connected_person: A proposed resolution applicant is either the applicant itself or a person connected with the applicant in a way relevant to the resolution process.
predicates.statutory_resolution_disqualification_ap: The proposed applicant or connected person falls within a statutory category that bars participation as a resolution applicant.

issues.definition: When a person applying to participate, or a relevant connected person, falls within a statutory disqualification during an insolvency resolution process, that applicant is excluded.

issues.legal_issue: During a corporate insolvency resolution process, a court should not order an interim preferential distribution to one class of creditors at the expense of other creditors and the collective resolution process.
material_facts: Money deposited during the proceedings was held by the Court while the corporate insolvency resolution process was pending.
Some home buyers sought refunds and requested that the deposited money be distributed to them on a pro-rata basis.
Most of the home buyers sought possession rather than refunds, and secured creditors had claims against the corporate debtor's assets.
The Court considered that distributing the money to the refund-seeking group would prefer that group and could prejudice other creditors and a composite resolution plan.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to direct a pro-rata interim disbursement to the home buyers seeking refunds and directed that the deposited money remain invested pending directions in the insolvency process.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, during the corporate insolvency resolution process, a preferential payment to a particular class of financial creditors would be impermissible and could cause injustice to other creditors. The process under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, requires a composite approach to the corporate debtor's financial situation. No earlier cases were relied on for this ruling.

predicates.corporate_insolvency_process_pending: A corporate insolvency resolution process remains pending.
predicates.creditor_group_seeks_interim_distributio: A group of creditors asks for money held in connection with the debtor to be distributed before the resolution process is complete.
predicates.distribution_would_prefer_that_group_ove: The proposed distribution would give one creditor group an advantage over other creditors or prejudice a collective resolution.

issues.definition: While a corporate insolvency process is pending, an interim distribution sought by one creditor group is denied when it would prefer that group over other creditors.

issues.legal_issue: The banking regulator may direct banks to initiate insolvency resolution proceedings against a debtor when the required authorization and regulatory recommendation are in place.
material_facts: The banking regulator asked to be permitted to direct banks to initiate corporate insolvency resolution proceedings against a holding company.

The company had been classified as a non-performing asset, and the regulator's advisory committee had recommended that it be referred for insolvency proceedings after no viable resolution plan was found.
The Central Government had authorized the regulator to issue directions concerning insolvency resolution for defaults under the insolvency law.
issues.conclusion: The Court permitted the regulator to direct the banks to initiate corporate insolvency resolution proceedings against the holding company.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 35AA and 35AB of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, as amended, empower the Central Government to authorize the Reserve Bank of India to issue directions to banking companies to initiate insolvency resolution proceedings and to issue directions concerning resolution of stressed assets. The Court relied on R.K. Garg v. Union of India, Peerless General Finance and Investment Co. Ltd. v. RBI, and T.N. Generation and Distribution Corporation Ltd. v. CSEPDI-Trishe Consortium for the principle that the Reserve Bank of India has expertise in economic and financial policy.

predicates.banking_regulator_seeks_insolvency_refer: A banking regulator asks to direct banks to refer a debtor for insolvency proceedings.
predicates.debtor_is_classified_as_non_performing: The debtor's account has been classified as a non-performing asset.
predicates.no_viable_resolution_plan_found: No viable resolution plan has been found for the debtor.

issues.definition: When a banking regulator seeks an insolvency referral for a debtor classified as non-performing and no viable resolution plan has been found, the regulator may direct the referral.
